person noun

in grammar

also first person, second person, third person, grammatical person, what person is it?

classical

Quint. 1.4.27: ut ignōret genera et quālitātēs et persōnās et numerōs
Varr. LL 8.20 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 226, 248

persōna, persōnae f.

noun, first declension

a grammatical person

Varro gives the three: the one who speaks, the one spoken to, the one spoken of. First person is prīma persōna (Quint. 1.6.15), second secunda, third tertia; the question is Cujus persōnae est? (Traupman 238).

Examples

  • quom item persōnārum nātūra triplex esset, quī loquerētur, ad quem, dē quō

    since the nature of persons was likewise threefold: who was speaking, to whom, about whomVarr. LL 8.20 (Lewis & Short)

  • nam praeteritō quidem tempore variē fōrmārī verba prīmā persōnā o litterā terminata, ipsa analogia cōnfiteātur

    for analogy itself would admit that verbs ending in o in the first person form their perfect in various waysQuint. 1.6.15

  • Cujus est persōnae? — Prīmae persōnae.

    What person is it? — First person.Traupman 238

See also verb, pronoun, impersonal verb.
